The engineering challenge of those gates though. The video shows a length of 50 foot between gates. If we say it was 15 wide and 15 feet tall times the length and times about 62 lbs per cubic foot of water we get almost 700000 lbs of water pressing against each gate when they are closed. double when one is open. Now try moving the gate with that much water pressure. Now keep a gate in moving condition while still keeping the seal. Even a tiny leak would shoot water out in jet like fashion quickly destroying the seal and the entire affair.

Maybe they moved the blocks to the build site like he thinks and maybe they even lifted them a small distance upwards near the pyramid but hard to believe they could do it on the scale he shows.

Edit

So if the heaviest block in the pyramid is about 400 tons then when a gate is open and there is about 700 tons of weight going against a gate when the gate above it is open, then how would they make a gate that could hold that much?

Also if there is a slight leak in a gate, even a pin prick, then the rules of hydrostatic pressure tell us that between chambers the pressure will compound on the last gate. Even the flex in the gates with no water transferred would be enough.

Also the masonry would have to be air tight. This was an era of dry stone masonry, and for a very very long time afterward.

Also how would the gate itself be liftable without it's interface with the chambers compromising an air tight seal? Movement in area physically isolated from you is a hard problem.
